name: xTool D1 Pro 40W
tagline: 40W Top D1 Pro module: strongest open-frame xTool diode
tldr: The 40W D1 Pro module swaps onto the same frame as 5W–20W heads. Best cut headroom in the line; verify optical power on the listing.

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cannot: Clear acrylic cutting (diode light passes through)

pros: Strongest cut headroom in the line: about 10 mm basswood-class stock in benchmarks
40W: the most cut-focused head in the xTool D1 Pro line
Swappable head on the same chassis: upgrade power without replacing the whole machine
Open-frame: plan laser glasses, exhaust, and workspace rules from day one
cons: Clear cast acrylic and thick production cutting still favor CO₂, not diode power alone
Confirm optical wattage on the listing before you buy
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 40W SKU on xTool D1 Pro. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Treat engraving and cutting as separate profiles. Push cut speeds only after test squares on your material. Compare CO₂ only when clear acrylic or all-day production enters the picture.
mainObjective: Maximum cut speed and depth in the line: engraving remains strong at tuned speeds

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable diode modules on D1 Pro frame
moduleSystem.description: xTool D1 Pro uses plug-in diode modules (5W–40W depending on era and listing). Buy the module power you need: same rail and software as other D1 Pro heads.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 40W diode module is the most cut-focused head on xTool D1 Pro: thicker basswood and faster fills than entry modules on the same chassis.
editorialDepth.limitations: Overkill if you only do fine engraving. Still a diode: clear cast acrylic means CO₂. Plan glasses and exhaust if the chassis is open-frame.
